question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=4-{t}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=4-{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=3,\,p(0)=4,\,p(-1)=3.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(0)p(0)+p(-1)p(-1)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(0)]^{2}+[p(-1)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(4)^{2}+(3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$
